questions.q: Ethanamide (CH₃CONH₂) is reduced with LiAlH₄ in dry ether followed by water work-up. The product is:
questions.explain: LiAlH₄ turns the amide C=O into CH₂ and keeps every carbon, giving CH₃CH₂NH₂. Methylamine (one carbon fewer) is the Hofmann bromamide product, the usual trap.

questions.q: Methyl isocyanide (CH₃–NC) is reduced with LiAlH₄. The product is:
questions.explain: In an isocyanide the carbon of NC ends up as a methyl group on nitrogen, giving the 2° amine CH₃–NH–CH₃. The isomeric nitrile CH₃CN would give the 1° amine ethylamine.

questions.q: What does nitrobenzene give with LiAlH₄?
questions.explain: Aromatic nitro compounds give azo compounds with metal hydrides, so aniline is made with Sn/HCl or catalytic hydrogenation. Aliphatic nitro compounds, by contrast, are reduced to amines.

questions.q: Ethyl but-3-enoate, CH₂=CH–CH₂–COOC₂H₅, is treated with LiAlH₄ and then H₃O⁺. The products are:
questions.explain: LiAlH₄ reduces the ester to the primary alcohol plus R′OH; the isolated C=C has no polarity for hydride to attack, so it survives. The aldehyde intermediate cannot be isolated with LiAlH₄.
